sentences: This bill is part of a package that changes the tax treatment of excess non-concessional contributions to superannuation.

The package would remove the excess non-concessional contributions tax when individuals withdraw the excess from superannuation, with associated earnings taxed at the individual's marginal rate and a 15% non-refundable tax offset available.
The tax would still apply to excess contributions that remain in the superannuation plan.
changes: Removes the excess non-concessional contributions tax for individuals who withdraw the excess and associated earnings from superannuation.
Includes associated earnings in assessable income taxed at the individual's marginal rate with a 15% non-refundable tax offset.
Imposes the excess non-concessional contributions tax on excess contributions left in the superannuation plan.
summary.affected: Individuals who make excess non-concessional contributions to superannuation.

speeches.speaker: Steven Ciobo
speeches.brief: Moved that the Excess Exploration Credit Tax Bill 2014 be read a second time, explaining that it would recover Commonwealth costs when exploration companies distributed more credits than permitted under the Exploration Development Incentive.

speeches.speaker: Graham Perrett
speeches.brief: Traced the history of compulsory superannuation from the Whitlam government to today, noting the accumulated superannuation pool reached $1.9 trillion, equivalent to 117 per cent of GDP, and said only 1,940 taxpayers, mostly earning under $50,000, breached the non-concessional contributions cap, with a median breach of $5,876.

speeches.speaker: George Christensen
speeches.brief: Backed the Exploration Development Incentive, capped at $100 million over three years, accused Labor and the Greens of waging a 'class war' on mining after their minerals resource rent tax aimed to raise $11 billion from 'superprofits', and argued expanding coal exports could help lift some of the 1.2 billion people worldwide who lack access to electricity out of energy poverty.

speeches.speaker: Josh Frydenberg
speeches.brief: Summed up the tax bill's seven schedules, thanked the opposition for not opposing it, and noted several measures, including the capital gains tax exemptions for compensation and insurance and for superannuation fund mergers, implement previously announced but unenacted Labor policies.
